text:
maya: headsup — Cypress sees number formatting regressions after we applied their LoRA to redwood/7b-int3. Quick repro attached.

maya: local repro: `rwi serve --model redwood/7b-int3 --patch cypress-lora-v2 && curl -sS localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"Invoice total: $", "max_tokens":10}'`

maya: example output: "Invoice total: $ 12,00.00" (expected "1,200.00"). Happens intermittently with 4+ digit amounts.

samir: thanks. First hypothesis: the graft merge + int3 quant minor shifts logits for comma vs digit tokens. Can we run a tiny eval pack to confirm? :mag_right:

maya: launched eval-1788881234-mini (50 invoice examples).

eval-bot: EVAL eval-1788881234-mini
variant: redwood/7b-int3 + cypress-lora-v2 (graft)
metric: amount-exact-match 79/100
observed: comma insertion errors concentrate on thousands separators

zhen: baseline 7b-int3 (no patch) on same set = 98/100. Delta ~19 pts.

oliver: ouch. Two quick experiments: (A) rebake patch with post-quant calibration (calib O2) and (B) stitch-merge (warm-start) to preserve pre-merge logit priors.

samir: also request deterministic decode traces. maya, can you run temp=0 top_k=1 logprobs=16 on 3 failing IDs and paste logits?

maya: done. sample trace: 
```nEX id cyp-078
prompt: "Invoice total: $"
gold: "1200.00"
decode: tokens ["1","200",".","00"]
step2 logits(top3): {",": -0.15, "12": -1.7, "1": -0.4}
note: "," favored -> produces 1,200 form; downstream reconcat/tokenize sometimes yields 12,00
```

zhen: that matches the hypothesis. I'll rebake with quant calibration and run mini eval.

maya: rebake+calib quick-run: eval-1788881234-rebake -> amount-exact-match 94/100. Many comma issues resolved, a few left for non-standard separators.

oliver: good sign. zhen, please queue a larger focused eval (500 invoices, mixed locales) comparing three variants: baseline, graft-rebake, stitch-merge. Tag seeds + decode params.

zhen: queued eval-1788881234-full on gpu-7; est runtime ~100m. Will include CSV of failures and per-locale breakdown.

eval-bot: queued eval-1788881234-full; progress updates will be posted here. :robot_face:

samir: acceptance criteria for customer: if rebake <=3pt gap vs baseline on Cypress-critical parsers -> recommend rebake pipeline. If stitch outperforms rebake significantly -> consider updating merge docs to prefer stitch for numeric-heavy LoRAs.

maya: drafting a short note to support-cypress: "We've reproduced the formatting drift. Root cause: small logit nudges amplified by int3 quant causing comma token preference. Interim: we recommend rebake+quant-calibration; stitch-merge is an alternative. We're running full eval and will share detailed numbers and a migration checklist."

support-cypress: thanks — we can also upload a handful of edge-case invoices (thin-space, non-breaking space, local currency separators). Dropping them into the upload bucket now.

oliver: if residual locale-specific failures persist we can ship a short-term post-processing sanitizer that normalizes separators before numeric parsing. Also adding numeric-format tests to onboarding eval packs to catch this earlier.

zhen: full run completed: summary (excerpt) -> baseline 498/500, graft-rebake 485/500, stitch-merge 492/500. Per-locale: en_US gap closed to 1pt; some CJK/KR separators still off in graft variants. CSV with example IDs uploaded to /evals/1788881234/results.csv.

maya: thanks — i'll update the customer note with numbers and recommended pipeline: rebake+calib as default, stitch if they prefer warm-start fidelity. Also documenting required regression checks in onboarding playbook.

samir: nice work. i'll open a short RFC to add numeric-format testcases to the LoRA onboarding checklist and add a knob in our merge tool to prefer stitch for adapters flagged as numeric-sensitive.

eval-bot: artifacts uploaded: /evals/1788881234/{results.csv,logits-samples.json,run-config.yaml}.

oliver: great. closing the loop — ping me if Cypress wants a conference call to walk through the changes. :white_check_mark:
